page: Vultr vcg-a40-8c-40g-16vram is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine featuring a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU with 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. The instance is powered by an Intel x86_64 processor configured with 8 shared vCPUs, consisting of 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core, running at 2.0 GHz. It includes 40.0 GB of system memory, providing 5.0 GB per core, and is equipped with 740 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark data indicates average-tier CPU and memory performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 14175.12 and a PassMark CPU score of 14090.9. However, its GPU-accelerated capabilities deliver top-tier performance in LLM inference workloads. For a small 135M model, it achieves prompt processing speeds of 9944.32 tokens per second and text generation speeds of 464.42 tokens per second. For a medium 7B model, it sustains prompt processing at 3147.67 tokens per second and text generation at 107.73 tokens per second.

This server offers a cost-effective entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads by utilizing a fractional GPU allocation paired with shared CPU resources. This resource density makes it highly suitable for mid-sized machine learning inference, data science prototyping, and database operations, while avoiding the higher costs associated with full, dedicated GPU instances.
